extracted.intended_audience: general public and stakeholders (landowners, researchers, conservation partners, NGOs, policymakers)
extracted.subtask_description: A public-facing overview of the U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service's Endangered Species Act program, describing tools, activities, and participation pathways used to conserve and recover imperiled species. Intended to inform and direct stakeholders to programs, documents, news, and opportunities for involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modernize ESA implementation using conservation tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Recovery efforts should be made more efficient and effective by working with others to invigorate and modernize implementation of the ESA using current conservation tools and developing new ones at every opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text emphasizes both using existing tools and developing new tools to improve conservation and recovery outcomes; the objective is efficiency and effectiveness of recovery efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of key conservation tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Major tools that play a part in achieving conservation and recovery goals include interagency consultations, incentives for landowners and managers to engage in voluntary conservation partnerships, grants, and permits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explicitly lists: 'interagency consultations; incentives for landowners and managers to engage in voluntary conservation partnerships; grants to states and territories, private landowners, and conservation groups; and permits that authorize scientific research ... or activities that enhance the propagation or survival of listed species.' These are presented as central mechanisms for implementing recovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interagency consultations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use interagency consultation processes as a tool in ESA implementation and recovery activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed by the agency as a primary tool; implies coordination across federal (and possibly state/local) agencies to assess and mitigate impacts to listed species and habitat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentives for landowners and voluntary conservation partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide incentives for landowners and managers to voluntarily engage in conservation partnerships that support listed and candidate species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page highlights incentives as a major tool to encourage non-federal partners to protect habitat and participate in recovery efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants to support conservation projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide grants to states, territories, private landowners, and conservation groups to fund conservation projects that further recovery objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants are named as a central mechanism; intended recipients include governmental jurisdictions and private actors working on conservation projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permits for research and enhancement activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Issue permits that authorize scientific research to learn more about listed species, or activities that enhance propagation or survival of listed species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits are described as authorizing either scientific study or enhancement-of-survival activities, enabling actions that support recovery while being regulated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listing and critical habitat designation
rubrics_metrics.description: List species under the Endangered Species Act and designate critical habitat as fundamental steps in conserving and recovering species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency identifies species listing and critical habitat designation as core aspects of its work; these actions trigger protections and inform recovery planning and regulatory measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop protective regulations for threatened species
rubrics_metrics.description: When species are listed as threatened, develop and implement protective regulations (including potential 4(d) rules) to tailor protections appropriate to the species' needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page cites an example: proposing threatened status with a 4(d) rule (Borneo earless monitor), indicating regulatory tailoring for threatened listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop and implement recovery plans; monitor and evaluate status
rubrics_metrics.description: Create and carry out recovery plans for listed species, including ongoing monitoring and evaluation of species' status and recovery progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists 'developing and implementing recovery plans for listed species, monitoring and evaluating the status of listed species' and cooperative development of conservation plans with non-federal partners as core program activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisions based on the best available science
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the best available science when reviewing species status and making listing/delisting determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Roanoke logperch delisting example states: 'After reviewing the best available science, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service has determined the Roanoke logperch ... will be removed,' indicating that scientific evidence is the standard for status decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public engagement and opportunity for comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek public comment and hold informational meetings to inform and solicit input on proposed agreements and recovery actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include seeking public comment on a proposed nationwide Conservation Benefit Agreement for bumble bees and holding virtual informational meetings on recovery programs; these demonstrate mechanisms for public involvement in decision-making.
